title: The Game Boy Almost Shipped With Mario Instead of Tetris
hook: In 1989 Nintendo of America's president wanted Mario in every Game Boy box, until one man told him Tetris would sell to everyone. That cartridge went on to sell 35 million copies. Which game came in your Game Boy box?

script: Did you know the Game Boy almost shipped with Mario in the box instead of Tetris? Back in nineteen eighty nine, Nintendo of America president Minoru Arakawa wanted to pack in Mario with the new handheld. Then a game publisher named Henk Rogers showed up holding the handheld rights to Tetris. He told Arakawa that Tetris belonged in every Game Boy box. Arakawa asked why he would include Tetris when he already had Mario. Rogers answered with a line that is now famous. If you want little boys to buy your Game Boy, pack in Mario. If you want everyone to buy your Game Boy, pack in Tetris. He added that Nintendo could still sell Mario on its own afterward and make even more money. Arakawa agreed. The Game Boy reached North America that July, and Tetris was inside every box. That version of Tetris went on to sell about thirty five million copies. Across its whole life, the Game Boy family passed one hundred eighteen million systems sold worldwide. And the handheld is back in the news this week. Nintendo confirmed three more Game Boy games arrive on Switch Online on October twenty seventh, including Mole Mania, a puzzle game produced by Shigeru Miyamoto. So which game was in your Game Boy box? Follow for more gaming history.
